title: Use React Flow built-in colorMode prop instead of manual CSS overrides
description: React Flow v12 (we use ^12.6.0) has a built-in colorMode prop that handles dark mode for all internal elements (edges, controls, minimap, background, selection box, connection line) automatically via CSS variables. The project currently uses ~40 lines of manual CSS overrides in index.css (.dark .react-flow__controls, .dark .react-flow__background, .dark .react-flow__edge-path, .dark .react-flow__minimap, etc.) to achieve the same effect. Replace these with: <ReactFlow colorMode={effectiveTheme} ...> where effectiveTheme comes from useThemeStore().getEffectiveTheme(). This simplifies maintenance, ensures complete dark mode coverage for all React Flow internals (including selection rectangles and connection lines that may be missed by manual CSS), and uses the library's native theming system. After adding colorMode prop, remove the manual .dark .react-flow__* rules from index.css. Keep the custom focus-visible styles since those are project-specific accessibility enhancements.
